atAGlance: Bê thui is tender young veal, often linked with Quảng Nam/Cầu Mống style, served with herbs, rice paper, and pungent mắm nêm fermented anchovy dip.
whatItIs: Bê thui is lightly roasted young veal served for wrapping with rice paper, herbs, green banana, star fruit, and mắm nêm. The fermented anchovy dip is strong, salty, and central.
howToEnjoy: Wrap veal with herbs and rice paper, then dip lightly in mắm nêm. Start carefully; fermented anchovy dip is powerful and salty.
howLocalsOrder: Order bê thui as a shared wrap-and-dip plate. Ask for extra bánh tráng, extra herbs, or nước chấm if mắm nêm feels too strong.
worthKnowing: Bê thui is strongly associated with Quảng Nam and Cầu Mống-style veal, a central Vietnamese specialty travelers may see near Đà Nẵng and Hội An.
goodToKnow: Mắm nêm is fermented anchovy dip, not tamarind. It can be funky, salty, and intense.
commonOptions: nước chấm instead of mắm nêm
travelerCaution: Contains veal and often fermented anchovy sauce.
